body.en:
Question B-006-006-009.

Why the correct answer is right: When the antenna impedance already matches the line characteristic impedance, the line is terminated correctly and its length does not change the match.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "must be a full wavelength long": A full-wavelength line repeats impedance, but that special length is unnecessary when the antenna is already correctly matched to the line.
- sourceIndex 2: "must be an odd number of quarter-wavelengths": Odd quarter-wave lengths are used for intentional impedance transformation in some systems; they are not required for a line that is already matched.
- sourceIndex 3: "must be an even number of half-wavelengths": Even half-wavelengths repeat the load impedance at the input, but a matched load is matched through any practical line length.
